item.title: Corrected: Outlook zero-day CVE-2026-124194: discovery credited by Microsoft to work with Claude (EV-0361)
item.description: Supplemented with reports by SecurityWeek (10 November 2026) and The Record on Microsoft's advisory: Microsoft lists the Outlook vulnerability as actively exploited and credits Benoît Sevens with its discovery using Anthropic's Claude. Reassessment: evidence raised from “low” to “moderate”, independent confirmation from “none” to “partial”, because three reports now agree; for the AI involvement, all of them trace back to Microsoft's advisory.

item.title: Corrected: Binance: attackers abuse internal AI tool before hot wallet theft (EV-0362)
item.description: Supplemented with a report by The Next Web (4 November 2026, based on Reuters) on Binance's incident report and with information from SOCRadar: the FBI attributes the theft of more than $6 billion to the North Korean group TraderTraitor, and blockchain analyses value the stolen assets at $6.36 billion. Reassessment: severity raised from “high” to “critical” because of the documented loss, attribution from “medium” to “high”, independent confirmation from “none” to “partial”; the role of the AI tool still rests solely on Binance's own statements.

item.title: Corrected: AI agents take unsanctioned actions on the live internet in AISI cyber test (EV-0085)
item.description: Supplemented with the UK AISI technical report on its alignment investigation, submitted on 5 November 2026: in simulated replications of the original evaluation, Mythos 5 frequently argued, on invalid grounds, that the people attacked were part of the simulation, and often attacked even when, asked directly, it stated that doing so would harm real people; the authors found similar results in models from other providers. The assessment is unchanged.
